request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A PENDING claim is now bound by a statement like any other claim that counts: while a statement

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A PENDING claim is now bound by a statement like any other claim that counts. But `bin/e2e` still shows **3 passed, 1 failed**. The failing test ("pending bound scenario 1") fails on a parent-sheet rate shown in an as-of view, which this change doesn't touch.

**What changed**
- `Claim.java`: `isBound()` and `due()` no longer make an exception for PENDING. A bound PENDING claim shows and totals the figure its statement bound. The same figure is used when the claim is settled, approved, rejected back to OPEN or re-stated, and in rate previews.
- Front end: `isBound` in `features/claims/api.ts` and the due figure in `features/rates/api.ts` no longer exclude PENDING, so the screen matches the server.
- Updated the comments in `ApproveClaim.java` and `RejectClaim.java` to match.

**Why scenario 1 still fails**
It stops at `acceptance.spec.ts:322`, which expects `rate-current-C` to show `5.00` in the as-of 2026-04-02 view; the app shows `n/a`.
- **Not caused by this change.** I reverted my edits, rebuilt, and it failed at the same line.
- **The cause is the real date.** The test sets "today" on the child sheet but not on the parent sheet (`${sheet}-p`). A new sheet's today is the real date, so the parent's rates are recorded as set on 2026-11-15. The as-of view only counts rates set on or before 2026-04-02, so it hides them. The expected `5.00` (the parent's rate) only appears if the test runs before April 2026, which is probably when the spec was written. Line 385 (`rate-month-C-2026-04`) fails for the same reason.
- **The rest of the scenario passes.** I ran a temporary copy of the spec that also set the parent sheet's today to 2026-03-20, and all 4 tests passed. The copy is deleted and the real spec is unchanged.

I didn't change how the as-of view handles rates just to satisfy a test that depends on the real date. Doing so would break the rule that a view shows things as they stood on that date. It could be made to pass by running the suite with the clock set before April 2026, or by updating the spec to set the parent sheet's today. I wasn't allowed to edit the spec, so that call is yours.

One note: this sandbox uses `PORT=3001`, and a different app is running on port 3000, so manual Playwright runs need `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001`.
